result:
Got all main sites. Have full picture now — util itself well-tested and safe. All call sites just UI label truncation, low-risk. Rank confidence by call correctness.

**`truncate_and_trailoff`** (`crates/util/src/util.rs:58`) — char-safe, unit-tested (`util.rs:847-854`), handles UTF-8 boundaries right, `debug_assert!(max_chars >= 5)`.

Callers, confidence high→low:

| Site | Call | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| `util.rs` tests | direct unit tests | **Max** — tests func itself |
| `editor/items.rs:770,784` | tab title, `MAX_TAB_TITLE_LEN=24` (≥5) | **High** |
| `title_bar.rs:730,878` | project/branch name, len=40 | **High** |
| `search/project_search.rs:661` | query tab title, `MAX_TAB_TITLE_LEN` | **High** |
| `git_ui/blame_ui.rs:44` | author name, len=20 | **High** |
| `git_ui/picker_prompt.rs:220` | fuzzy match label, `max_chars` param (70 or 34, caller-set, ≥5) | **High** |
| `agent/tools/update_title_tool.rs:96` | title, `MAX_TITLE_LEN=200` | **High** |
| `debugger_ui/dropdown_menus.rs:35,83,315` | labels, 150/50/150 | **High** |
| `terminal.rs:2162,2195,2196` | task/process labels, `MAX_CHARS=25` | **High** |
| `tasks_ui/modal.rs:529` | tags line, `MAX_TAGS_LINE_LEN` (check const ≥5) | **Med-high** — didn't verify const val, but pattern safe |
| `agent_ui/thread_view.rs:1461` | msg text→title, hardcoded 200 | **High** |
| `activity_indicator.rs:668` | msg, `MAX_MESSAGE_LEN=50` | **High** |
| `activity_indicator.rs:579` | `MAX_MESSAGE_LEN.saturating_sub(health_str.len())` — **could go below 5**, hits `debug_assert!` panic in debug builds if `health_str` long (server name + "Warning: ") | **Low** — only real risk found |
| `git_ui/commit_view.rs:935` | hardcoded `20` for commit subject | **High** but tight margin (just above assert floor) |

Only weak spot: `activity_indicator.rs:579` — `saturating_sub` can produce a value <5 if server name is long, triggering `debug_assert!` in debug builds (panic) or fine in release (silent no-op guard skipped since no clamp). Worth flag if you hit debug crashes there.
